items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: Say, 'Man, come on and go down ever to my job with me.' I say, 'Your job?' He say, 'Yeah, down at the Three Deuces.'

ctx.x: Yes. It hurt him. So, I said, "Well, everyone sound great. I'm going back East, into the competition and see what is happening." 'Cause I didn't know what was happening. I wanted to go to New York, but every record that I heard that come out of New York, the soloists sounded like they were playing snakes, so I got cold feet and stopped in Chicago.

And my first job was with Lil Armstrong. And she was on one end -- we were playing the Bacon's Casino. And she was on one end of the bandstand, and the tenor player and the trumpet player and the drummer player was over on the other end of the bandstand. So I'm standing up there by her.

ctx.x: Then I went out to Chicago. Glaser sent me out to Chicago. Then it was pushing on to '41, and I went to the Capitol Lounge.

items.q: So when that job ended, Roy joined Krupa.

ctx.x: How did that come about that Roy Eldridge theme get to Hollywood?
He was with Krupa's band at the time.

items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: Everybody in the band, so they give him the name "the Ray."

ctx.x: No, I'm not hip to the ray.

He'll have his eyeglasses down on the tip of his nose, and he'd be looking at you, you know? You'd be reading the music. You'd have a feeling that he was looking at you, you raise up, he'd be looking at you. Giving you the ray. Everybody in the band, so they give him the name "the Ray." You know?

The band -- this was an experience, oh, boy. 'Cause I never should have got that thing. We had a tune -- I can't recall the name of it. Something about the sun, like, big preamble introduction, you know. And leave a bar out, and Big Sid would say, "Quit your squawking. I hear your talking," you know.
